title: Streaming PII ACK Coordinator and Consistent Tombstone Propagation
creator: Anika Shah
description: Introduce a lightweight coordinator service and ACK protocol for streaming PII tombstones so downstream consumers (analytics materializations, long-term backups, third-party sinks) can acknowledge deletion intent and the console backend can guarantee eventual consistency and auditability. This reduces blind spots where tombstones are produced but not applied, improving regulatory compliance and shortening incident resolution windows.
background: Currently we emit tombstone messages to the analytics Kafka topic and mark rows for deletion in the OLAP layer. We occasionally observe rehydration of deleted records in historical materializations and third-party exports due to missed tombstones during consumer replays or compact/retention windows. Existing deletion telemetry is sparse: we have producer-side metrics but no consumer-level ACK trail that ties a tombstone write to an applied deletion in each downstream system.
goals: Design an ACK protocol for tombstone propagation that is bootstrap-friendly for existing consumers.
Provide an idempotent, content-based tombstone identifier (consistent hash) so deletes are deterministic across replays.
Expose an audit trail and SLA for tombstone application per downstream sink and enable retries/backfills for missed deletions.
Minimize latency and cost overhead on the primary ingestion path and maintain compatibility with current schema evolution.
Document runbooks and automated remediation for missed ACKs.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator service accepts tombstone events from producer topic and emits tombstone metadata to 'pii-acks' topic within 50ms of receipt on 99th percentile.
Downstream consumers can send ACK messages referencing a consistent tombstone hash; coordinator records per-sink ACKs and surfaces missing acknowledgements in Console dashboards.
Backfill tool can scan materializations and emit corrective tombstones for sinks that missed deletion windows; end-to-end test demonstrates backfill correcting a seeded missed-delete scenario.
Audit export includes tombstone id, original event timestamp, sink status (acked/unacked), retries, and first-apply timestamp for compliance reporting.
No increase >5% in ingest p99 latency after coordinator opt-in in a canary environment.
Security review completed for tombstone metadata storage and access controls.
Documentation and runbook reviewed by Privacy and Compliance teams.
Automated alerting triggers if any high-volume sink has >0.1% unacked tombstones for 24 hours.
design_notes: Use a content-addressable tombstone id: SHA-256 over a stable canonicalization of pii_key + deletion_reason + generation_epoch. This id is stable across replays and schema-additive changes. Tombstone metadata will be compact (id, original_event_ts, producer_offset, canonical_key, optional retention_exemption_flag). Coordinator persists only metadata and last-seen ACK per sink to a compacted RocksDB state or DynamoDB table (configurable per deployment). Communication pattern: producer -> primary topic (existing), tombstone filter service forwards to coordinator synchronously, coordinator writes tombstone-metadata to 'pii-acks' topic. Consumers can either listen to 'pii-acks' to pull tombstone metadata or continue to derive id locally and push ACKs to 'pii-acks-acks' topic. Avoid duplicating payloads to keep throughput costs low.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype coordinator as a sidecar service in canary cluster. Implement tombstone id generator and basic ACK storage (local RocksDB).
Phase 2: Add 'pii-acks' topic and define Avro schema for tombstone metadata + ack message. Instrument producer path to forward tombstone to coordinator.
Phase 3: Update two consumer types in staging: (a) OLAP materializer (BigQuery/ClickHouse) to emit ACK after apply, (b) S3 sink to confirm logical deletion or expunge.
Phase 4: Implement backfill tool that cross-checks historical materializations against coordinator state and emits corrective tombstones; create dry-run mode to estimate impact.
Phase 5: Put coordinator behind feature flag; run 10% traffic canary; validate metrics and alerts; iterate.
Phase 6: Run security review, finalize IAM roles for coordinator metadata reads/writes and Console UI access.
Phase 7: Full rollout and deprecation plan for any ad-hoc deletion scripts.
rollout_plan: Canary (10%): coordinator sidecar in us-west-2, opt-in tag on a subset of tenants; verify ingestion latency and ack rates for those tenants.
Scale to 50% after 72 hours if no regression; run targeted backfills for a handful of historic missed-delete incidents to validate recovery paths.
Full rollout to all regions with coordinator replicated per-region; enable default automatic tombstone forwarding after parity checks.
Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring phase with weekly compliance reports to Privacy team.
Rollout gates: consumer client libraries updated OR consumer shim deployed; security review green; 0 critical SLO regressions in canary.
qa_plan: Unit tests for tombstone id canonicalization and collision resistance checks.
Integration test that emits tombstones, simulates consumer apply, posts ACK, and validates coordinator state and audit export.
Chaos test: replay topic with duplicated tombstones and out-of-order delivery to validate idempotency and ACK semantics.
Performance test: measure coordinator p99 latency at intended production throughput (peak throughput test harness included).
Compliance test: run audit export and verify all fields required by legal are present and immutable once emitted.
Runbook drill: simulate sink outage and run documented remediation to ensure backfill recovers missed deletes.
risks: Producer path added synchronous step could increase ingest latency if coordinator becomes a bottleneck — mitigated via async forward and local write-ahead log.
Downstream sinks with no ability to emit ACKs (closed third-party integrations) will require connector shims or manual reconciliation.
Storage cost for ACK state could grow with number of tenants and sinks; will use TTL/compaction and retention policies to bound cost.
Mis-canonicalization of keys could lead to mismatched tombstone ids; plan to include a migration checker and dual-write compatibility window.
Operational complexity: new alerting and SLA for unacked tombstones requires on-call runbook updates and PagerDuty playbooks.
